strengths: Strong theoretical contributions: Proposition 1 provides elegant ELBO decomposition; Corollary 2 shows the bound becomes tight with perfect encoders for arbitrary modality counts, unlike mixture-based bounds with increasing gaps; Remark 5 makes this advantage precise

Well-motivated architectural innovations using permutation-invariant networks (DeepSets, Transformers) with principled theoretical justification via Bloem-Reddy & Teh (2020); clean extension to permutation-equivariant schemes for private latents

Comprehensive experimental validation across linear Gaussians, non-linear identifiable models, and real images (MNIST-SVHN-Text) with multiple metrics and ablations; extensive implementation details support reproducibility

Information-theoretic perspective connecting to rate-distortion; formal identifiability results (Proposition 15) extending iVAE theory to multi-modal conditionals; practical considerations for missing modalities and mixture priors
weaknesses: Critical ambiguity in theoretical claims: the 'approximate lower bound' status is unclear—when the KL term ∫pd(x)qϕ(z|x)[log(qϕ(z|xS)/pθ(z|xS))]dzdx is positive, the bound is not a valid lower bound. Corollary 2's gap depends on encoder quality but lacks analysis of approximation error under finite capacity

Mixed empirical results undermine practical claims: on MNIST-SVHN-Text, mixture bounds are competitive/superior on conditional coherence (Table 6); LLH improvements are modest (~5-15%); Table 1 shows learnable aggregation helps marginally (0.06% vs 0.6%). No systematic analysis of when proposed approach outperforms baselines

Computational overhead inadequately addressed: gradient computation requires sampling from two distributions (acknowledged as 'more expensive'), but no runtime comparisons provided; scalability to high-M scenarios and practical computational costs unknown—a significant barrier to adoption

Optimization challenges underexplored: Remark 6 identifies conflicting gradients across modality masks but offers no solutions; masking distribution ρ selection lacks guidance; no convergence analysis, training stability discussion, or comparison of optimization difficulty vs. mixture bounds

Strong assumptions limit applicability: Proposition 15 requires exponential family and injective decoders, excluding discrete modalities and many practical VAE variants; theoretical results depend on encoders perfectly approximating posteriors—unrealistic in practice with finite-capacity networks

Limited novelty in components: PoE/MoE for multi-modal VAEs are established (Wu & Goodman 2018); DeepSets/Transformers are standard architectures; main contribution is combining these elements plus the new bound

Narrow experimental scope: largest experiments ~1M samples; all M≤5 modalities; missing modality handling (Section 4.3) discussed but not validated; unclear generalization to high-dimensional, many-modality settings; identifiability improvements sometimes marginal (MCC differences ~1-3%)
